q: A function f: X → Y between metric spaces is uniformly continuous if:
opts: For each x there exists δ>0 such that d(x,y)<δ implies d(f(x),f(y))<ε
There exists δ>0 depending only on ε such that d(x,y)<δ implies d(f(x),f(y))<ε for all x,y
f maps Cauchy sequences to convergent sequences
exp: Uniform continuity requires a single δ that works for all points simultaneously, unlike pointwise continuity where δ may depend on x.
